Container.Name: filearr-caddy
Container.Overview:
TLS reverse proxy for filearr — Caddy 2.11.4 built with the Cloudflare DNS-01 solver and the layer4 (raw TCP/SNI) app. OPTIONAL unless you want mutual-TLS agent authentication, which this container is the only supported way to get.
TWO PROFILES, chosen with FILEARR_CADDY_PROFILE: internal (default) — Caddy's own self-signed CA. Needs no domain, no DNS credentials and no internet: you get HTTPS on the LAN immediately, at the cost of trusting the generated root on each client. acme — a real Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate for *.<your domain> via the Cloudflare DNS-01 challenge (no inbound port 80 needed), serving THREE names: filearr.<domain> for the UI, agents.<domain> requiring a client certificate for the agent fleet, and ca.<domain> passed through raw to the filearr-stepca container.
NETWORKING: this template DEFAULTS to br0 — keep it, and set a FIXED IP below. Caddy must own its ports on an address of its own: on ANY bridge-type network (including the 'filearr' network) the 80/443 mappings publish to the HOST address, and Unraid's own web GUI already holds host port 80, so Apply fails with 'address already in use'. On br0 the mappings are ignored and the container's own IP serves 80/443 directly.
In the DEFAULT topology that makes this the one container on TWO networks — br0 for the LAN address, plus the 'filearr' network so App Upstream and CA Upstream resolve by name — and Unraid's single Network Type dropdown cannot express that. A manual 'docker network connect filearr filearr-caddy' takes effect at once but is DISCARDED every time Apply or an image update re-creates the container; the guide gives three ways to make it stick. If you would rather not dual-home, run the whole stack fully bridged on br0 and set the two upstreams below to LAN IPs — equally supported. https://pwsh.github.io/filearr/deployment/unraid/#dual-homing
HTTP/3 is deliberately not enabled: both configs pin h1+h2 because published 443 mappings are TCP-only, and QUIC would also bypass the raw ca.<domain> passthrough.
Container.Requires: filearr; docker network 'filearr'; filearr-stepca and a public domain if you use the acme profile

Config.Name: Profile
Config.Description: internal or acme. Start on internal to prove the proxy reaches filearr, then switch to acme once DNS and the Cloudflare token are ready. The acme profile refuses to start with a clear message if Domain, ACME Email or the Cloudflare token is missing, rather than serving a half-configured site.

Config.Name: HTTPS Port
Config.Description: Public HTTPS. IGNORED on br0 (the default) — the container's own IP serves 443 directly; the mapping matters only on a bridge-type network, where it will collide with anything already on the host's 443. TCP only by design — do not add a UDP mapping (see the HTTP/3 note in the overview).

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: IGNORED on br0 (the default). Only used by the acme profile for HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects. The certificate itself comes from the DNS-01 challenge, so nothing on the internet needs to reach this port. Safe to leave unmapped on the internal profile.

Config.Name: Compat HTTPS Port
Config.Description: OPTIONAL second HTTPS mapping, matching the docker-compose deployment's 8443. Only useful if you have existing bookmarks or agents pointed at that port. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: Certificates
Config.Description: Caddy's certificate store: the internal profile's self-signed root (which your clients trust) and the acme profile's issued Let's Encrypt certificates plus the ACME account key. Must persist — losing it re-issues everything and, on the internal profile, invalidates the root your clients already trust.

Config.Name: Caddy State
Config.Description: Caddy's autosave/runtime state. Small; keep it persistent so restarts are quiet.

Config.Name: step-ca Root (read-only)
Config.Description: Read-only view of the filearr-stepca Data path. The acme profile reads /step-root/certs/root_ca.crt as the trust pool for verifying agent client certificates. Point this at the SAME path as filearr-stepca's Data setting. Not used at all by the internal profile — remove it if you are not running the agent plane.

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: acme profile only. Your APEX zone, e.g. example.com — not a hostname. The wildcard certificate covers *.<domain> and the config serves filearr.<domain>, agents.<domain> and ca.<domain> off it. All three names must resolve to this container's IP.

Config.Name: ACME Email
Config.Description: acme profile only. Let's Encrypt account email — where expiry warnings go if renewal ever stops working.

Config.Name: Cloudflare API Token
Config.Description: SECRET, acme profile only. A Cloudflare API token scoped to Zone:DNS:Edit on this zone ONLY — it is used to publish the _acme-challenge TXT record. Do not use a Global API Key.

Config.Name: Proxy Shared Secret
Config.Description: SECRET. Stamped on X-Filearr-Proxy-Auth for requests arriving at agents.<domain>, so filearr knows the client certificate really was verified here and the identity headers are not forged. Must be byte-identical to the filearr container's Proxy Shared Secret. Generate: openssl rand -hex 32.

Config.Name: App Upstream
Config.Description: host:port of the filearr container. On the shared 'filearr' network that is the container NAME with the CONTAINER port 8000, not the 8484 host mapping, because this proxy talks over the internal network. On a fully bridged (br0) stack put the app container's fixed LAN IP here instead, still on port 8000 — a container with its own address publishes nothing through the host.

Config.Name: CA Upstream
Config.Description: host:port of the filearr-stepca container, for the raw ca.<domain> passthrough — the container name on the shared 'filearr' network, or its fixed LAN IP on a fully bridged (br0) stack. This connection is NOT TLS-terminated here on purpose: certificate renewal authenticates with the agent's own client certificate on the direct connection, and an L7 proxy silently breaks it.
